rows.name: From Connection to Impact: SINBON Builds "SINBON City" at electronica 2026, Hall A3, Booth 341
rows.description:
From Connection to Impact. Built Together.

For more than three decades, SINBON has been linking the things that matter. Through cables, connectors, and connectivity solutions, we have helped power, connect, and enable the technologies people rely on every day. Today, the conversation with our customers has changed. They are no longer looking only for components. They want partners who understand their challenges and can deliver solutions that create real, lasting impact across their industries and communities.
At electronica 2026, we invite you to step into the SINBON city, an immersive space where you can see how connectivity shapes the world around us, from the data centers behind AI to the devices that care for patients and move people through their cities.

Explore our latest solutions:
  • Customized Connectors — AI infrastructure, HPC & data centers 
  • EV Charging Cables — electric mobility
  • Diagnostic Imaging Cables — healthcare
  • Battery Swapping Cabinets — e-bikes & e-scooters
  • Industrial Robotics — automation & collaborative robots
Every one of these solutions reflects a simple belief: meaningful impact is never created alone. It is built together with our customers, our partners, and the communities we serve.

Visit us at electronica 2026 and let's build what's next, together.
  • Hall A3, Booth 341
  • November 10–13, 2026
  • Messe München, Germany

Come meet the SINBON team, explore what we have built, and discover what connection can make possible. We look forward to building the future with you.

rows.name: Joy Wu Receives Women’s Leadership Award at Miaoli Corporate Sustainability Excellence Award
rows.description:
The inaugural Miaoli Corporate Sustainability Excellence Award ceremony was held on August 24. Joy Wu, Vice President of SINBON’s Industrial BU, received the Women’s Leadership Award in recognition of her long-standing contributions to business management, team leadership, and talent development. The award recognizes not only her individual achievements but also reflects SINBON’s long-term commitment to developing talent and building strong teams.

Joy Wu began her career as a sales assistant and has since risen to become Vice President of the Industrial BU. With a background in the humanities, she started out in electronics sales and went on to take on roles as a Sales Engineer, Sales Manager, and Assistant Vice President. Through each role and new responsibility, she developed a deeper understanding of the industry, customers, and market, while steadily building her professional expertise and leadership capabilities. Over the years, she and her team have continued to expand the business, growing the Industrial BU from its early stages to more than NT$10 billion in annual revenue and establishing a presence across global markets.

This growth is about more than revenue. It reflects the trust built over the years through long-term relationships with customers, employees, and the market. With a clear sense of direction, Joy Wu leads her team while placing strong emphasis on talent development and organizational growth. She encourages people with different areas of expertise to make the most of their strengths, creating an environment where the team can take on challenges and move forward together.

At SINBON, talent has always been an important part of the company’s continued growth. Since its founding in 1989, SINBON has continued to expand its business in response to changing industry needs, serving industries including medical, automotive, green energy, industrial, and communication. Along the way, the company has not only built expertise across these fields but also developed managers and leaders capable of leading teams, taking on greater responsibilities, and contributing to the company’s continued growth.

rows.name: SINBON Electronics Chairman Joseph Wang Named to Harvard Business Review's Taiwan Top 100 CEOs for the Fourth Time
rows.description:
Joseph Wang, Chairman of SINBON Electronics, has been named to the 2026 Harvard Business Review (Complex Chinese edition) "Taiwan Top 100 CEOs" ranking, his fourth appearance on the list. Since first being named in 2020, SINBON's cumulative market value growth under his leadership has reached NT$63.8 billion, a personal career high, while average quarterly EPS has grown from NT$1.08 to NT$5.88.

The "Taiwan Top 100 CEOs" ranking is published every two years by Harvard Business Review's Complex Chinese edition and marks its sixth edition and tenth anniversary this year. It is Taiwan's largest survey, and the only one, focused on the individual long-term performance of listed-company leaders, evaluating executives on sustained financial performance, shareholder value, and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) outcomes over their tenure.

Commenting on the recognition, Wang said this honor belongs to every SINBON colleague, and to the customers, partners, and shareholders who have trusted the company along the way, not to him alone. He noted that in its more than 30 years, SINBON has chosen long-term value over short-term gains, adding that "a company's true competitiveness lies not only in technology, but in integrity, quality, and an unwavering commitment to customers."

Looking ahead, Wang said SINBON will continue investing in AI, humanoid robotics, energy transition, smart healthcare, and smart manufacturing, working closely with global customers and supply chain partners to build solutions that are safer and more sustainable. He added that the recognition is not only an honor but a responsibility: "I will keep working with our partners to create value, for the industry, for society, and for the next generation."
